site.name: Argentum-Juniata Mine
site.location: Base of east Aspen Mountain near Aspen
site.componentDetail: Silver-Lead-Zinc Mine Complex / Incline and Tunnel Workings
overview: The Argentum-Juniata was a major silver-era property at the base of east Aspen Mountain. Historic and mineral-resource records connect the property with the Juniata name, the Argenta Tunnel, the A-J Tunnel, and a group of claims and underground workings.

The identification point marks the documented Argentum-Juniata property and incline area. Historic maps and later records place related portals and workings close together, so it should not be read as a claim that one specific opening survives at that exact point.

timeline.text: A surviving Aspen Historical Society photograph documents the mine's compressor, boiler plant, and ore house.
The Argentum-Juniata operated during Aspen's major silver-mining period and was mapped as part of the district's connected underground mine network.
USGS Monograph 31 documented the geology and underground workings of the Aspen mining district, including the Argentum-Juniata property.
Federal mineral statistics reported siliceous silver ore with small lead values from the Argentum-Juniata.

moreHistory: Mineral-resource records list Argentum-Juniata Mine as the primary property name and treat Juniata, Argenta Tunnel, A-J Tunnel, and several named claims as associated names or workings.

The separately indexed Argentum-Juanita Incline lies only a short distance from the broader property coordinate and is treated here as a component of the same historic mine complex, not as an unrelated second destination.
The mine produced silver-bearing ore with lead and zinc associations. Period federal reporting specifically described its 1907 output as siliceous silver ore carrying small lead values.

Historic underground workings in Aspen are extensive and may intersect beneath developed areas. This entry identifies the historic property and does not imply access, ownership, or a safe surviving portal.
